title: RBAC V2 Collector Questions and Evidence Index
content:
Purpose and audience:

This is a working index to help Solutions/Trust/Platform teams answer customer security questionnaires and onboard SIEM collectors for RBAC v2 telemetry. Primary audiences: customer security reviewers, SRE/observability, solutions engineers, and compliance reviewers.

Status / quick context:
- Draft: consolidating answers and evidence pointers for common customer asks about RBAC v2, audit schema, SIEM export patterns, and evidence automation hooks.
- Goal: produce a 1-page customer-ready snapshot + a machine-readable evidence map for automation by EOY.

What this doc contains (high level):
1) Short answers for questionnaire sections we see repeatedly.
2) Index of evidence artifacts (where to find logs, config, and export samples).
3) Collector and SIEM integration notes (Splunk/Elastic/Chronicle examples).
4) Outstanding open questions and next actions.

1) Short-answer bank (concise, CISO-facing)
- RBAC model: RBAC v2 is hierarchical role-based access with explicit separation of Duties, time-bound role grants, and resource-scoped policies. Roles map to capabilities (read/write/admin) and are enforced at the API gateway and runtime enforcement points.
- Audit logging: All authorization decisions, role grant/revoke events, changes to role definitions, and sensitive configuration modifications are logged. Logs include actor, actor_identity_type, action, object_type, object_id, outcome, policy_version, request_id, and timestamp.
- Log retention & integrity: Audit logs are retained per customer plan (default 90 days for hosted), with longer retention available via Dedicated/Private. Logs are signed and pipeline checksums recorded to detect tampering; we also support continuous export to customer-controlled S3 for long-term retention.
- SIEM integration: We provide pre-built export adapters (JSON-over-HTTPS, syslog, and S3-batch) and recommended parsers for Splunk and Elastic. Exports include schema version metadata and sample event types for key workflows (authz_decision, role_change, api_error, admin_config_update).
- Evidence automation: Customers can request an evidence bundle (zip) of relevant audit slices by time range and filter (user, role, resource) via the support API. For enterprise customers we offer an automated webhook that posts evidence manifests to a customer endpoint.

2) Evidence index (where to pull artifacts)
- Audit log store (hosted): query via Console -> Audit -> export. Path: console.redwood.ai/audit/export (include customer org id).
- Raw log S3 (dedicated/private): s3://<customer-bucket>/redwood/audit/<org-id>/YYYY/MM/DD/*.json
- Role definitions: Git-backed role catalog (repo: infra/roles) with change history. PRs reference: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/roles.
- Policy engine config: stored in config service; snapshot available as JSON via admin API: GET /admin/policies?version=<v>.
- Evidence manifest example: a small JSONL file that lists event ids and S3 links (we attach to support tickets).

3) Audit log schema (concise spec) - sample fields and example event
- Minimal required fields (logging pipeline enforces presence):
  - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - event_id (uuid)
  - org_id
  - actor_id
  - actor_type (user|service|system)
  - action (e.g., authz_decision, role_grant, role_revoke, policy_update, login_failed)
  - resource_type (route, model, project, key)
  - resource_id
  - outcome (allowed|denied|error)
  - policy_version
  - request_id
  - service_region
  - raw_request_context (optional small JSON blob)

Example (plaintext single-line JSON event):
{
  "timestamp": "2025-09-09T14:23:05Z",
  "event_id": "3f9b6a3e-8b9d-4a7c-bf5a-2e4d1234f9b0",
  "org_id": "org-12345",
  "actor_id": "u-67890",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "action": "authz_decision",
  "resource_type": "route",
  "resource_id": "/v1/generate",
  "outcome": "denied",
  "policy_version": "rbac-v2-2025-07-31",
  "request_id": "req-4a5b6c7d",
  "service_region": "us-west-2"
}

4) SIEM collector patterns and example queries
- Splunk ingestion (http_event_collector): set up an HEC token, point our export job to the token endpoint, use index name redwood_audit_org_<org-id>.
- Example Splunk search to show denied authz in last 24h:
  index=redwood_audit_org_org-12345 action=authz_decision outcome=denied | stats count by actor_id, resource_id, policy_version
- Elastic ingest pipeline: add a processor to flatten raw_request_context, tag with _source.org_id, and apply index naming redwood-audit-YYYY.MM.DD. Example Kibana query:
  POST /redwood-audit-*/_search?q=action:authz_decision AND outcome:denied&size=50
- Chronicle/Carbon Black: deliver via syslog TLS or S3 export + remote ingest, include schema version header X-Redwood-Schema: 2025-09-01

5) Evidence automation hooks (implementation notes)
- /support/v1/evidence-request (internal API) accepts filters and returns an evidence manifest with presigned S3 links. Used by trust team to attach evidence to customer tickets.
- Webhook mode: enterprise orgs can register a POST URL and we will deliver manifests asynchronously (events: completed|failed).
- Automation TODO: add RBAC filters by role_name and role_change_correlation_id so auditors can retrieve role grant chains. JIRA SEC-9321 tracks work.

6) Common customer Qs & suggested one-line responses (for SEs)
Q: Can I see who changed a role and when?
A: Yes — role changes are captured in audit logs and in the roles Git catalog; we can provide a signed export for a requested time range.

Q: How do you ensure logs can't be altered?
A: Our pipeline records ingest checksums and stores signed manifests; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-side S3 with object-lock and KMS integration.

Q: Can I forward logs to my SIEM?
A: Yes — we support HEC, syslog TLS, and S3 export; we also provide parser templates for Splunk and Elastic.

7) Outstanding questions / risks
- Do we need an opt-in schema versioning header for every export (customer ask)? (owner: Marcus Li)
- Evidence export PII redaction: should we automatically mask certain fields for exports to non-customer endpoints? (owner: Nina Kapoor)
- Clarify retention SLAs for Dedicated customers vs hosted free tier — product to confirm with legal. (owner: Rajiv Menon)

8) Next steps and owners
- Create concise 1-page "RBAC v2 telemetry snapshot" for Trust Center (deadline: 2025-09-24) — owner: Evelyn Park.
- Add Splunk parser template to docs repo and link in Console UI (PR: infra/telemetry#PR-4567) — owner: Marcus Li.
- Wire up evidence-webhook demo for 2 pilot customers and get feedback (blocked by API rate limits) — owner: Rajiv Menon.

Attachments / references (working):
- internal confluence design: SECURITY/RBAC-V2-collector-spec
- jira: SEC-9321 (evidence automation backlog)
- github: infra/telemetry PR-4567 (splunk parser)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep customer language focused on capabilities and control; avoid promising features not implemented.
- For public Trust Center: strip operational details (exact S3 paths) and present sanitized examples.

Revision log:

- 2025-09-10 Marcus L: added Splunk/Kibana samples and open questions section.
